narrativeReportMd:
# DeviceMetric R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`DeviceMetric` remains the same resource identity, but the local content model changed substantially. The highest-impact breaks are the new mandatory modifier `status`, replacement of R4 `source`/`parent` with mandatory `device`, conversion of several primitive `code` fields to `CodeableConcept`, and replacement of `measurementPeriod` with `measurementFrequency`.

## Scope
I analyzed the R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions, package indexes and metadata, directly bound ValueSets/CodeSystems, status-related ConceptMaps, and the Device parent relationship for migration context. Inherited DomainResource/Resource changes are out of scope and are not counted as DeviceMetric findings.

## Main migration themes
R4 instances cannot be mechanically revalidated as R6 instances without structural transforms. R6 requires record lifecycle status and device linkage, while several existing coded primitives must become CodeableConcept objects with explicit coding systems. Several R6 concepts also lose clean R4 representation, especially `status`, `availability`, expanded colors, and free/extensible CodeableConcept codings.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-risk findings are `DeviceMetric:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:DeviceMetric.status:0d4f3a`, `DeviceMetric:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:DeviceMetric.device:7b61c0`, `DeviceMetric:TYPE_DOMAIN:DeviceMetric.category:19b7e1`, and `DeviceMetric:TERMINOLOGY_BINDING:DeviceMetric.color:3a91bd`. These affect validation, serializers/generated classes, REST summaries, and round-trip conversion.

## Findings requiring human review
Human policy is needed for deriving R6 `status`, deciding whether R4 `source` or `parent` should populate R6 `device`, preserving measurement cadence semantics, and mapping colors or extensible CodeableConcept content where no local ConceptMap exists.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several goals could have been less disruptive by adding optional elements while retaining old names/types for a transition period. The R6 design appears to align DeviceMetric with more explicit lifecycle status, device association, and richer terminology, but it is not wire-compatible with R4.

## Follow-up analysis
Base DomainResource changes, Device hierarchy migration, related SearchParameters, and missing terminology/conversion ConceptMaps should be handled by the relevant artifact or terminology reports.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `DeviceMetric` has multiple local breaking changes despite stable resource identity. Top concerns are mandatory `status`, mandatory `device` replacing R4 device-link fields, and primitive-code-to-CodeableConcept conversions with terminology changes. The main uncertainty is not whether the computable changes exist, but the intended migration policy for ambiguous mappings.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be treated as a transform, not a version relabel. R4 `category`, `color`, and calibration codes need to be wrapped as CodeableConcepts with appropriate coding systems; `measurementPeriod` must be reinterpreted as a Quantity frequency where possible; `source`/`parent` references need policy-driven consolidation into `device`; and all migrated resources need a new lifecycle `status`.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for element presence, cardinality, type, binding, flag, and local terminology changes because they are directly visible in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions and local CodeSystems. Confidence is medium for migration impact details where the local inputs lack official change notes, narrative migration guidance, and ConceptMaps for several replacements.

findings.title: R6 adds mandatory modifier `DeviceMetric.status` with no R4 element

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 DeviceMetric had `operationalStatus`, but no separate record lifecycle status element.

newState.summary: R6 requires `DeviceMetric.status` exactly once and marks it as a modifier.

binding.description: Describes the status of the DeviceMetric.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 introduces a new required lifecycle value set rather than reusing R4 operational status.

flags.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier in the R6 snapshot; `entered-in-error` means the resource should not be treated as valid clinical/device state.

semanticText.definition: Indicates current state of the record.
semanticText.comment: Unknown does not represent 'other' - one of the defined statuses must apply. Unknown is used when the authoring system is not sure what the current status is.

newState.narrativeMd: Every R6 DeviceMetric must now state record lifecycle status. This is distinct from whether the metric is operational.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A conformant R6 instance cannot omit `status`, while all R4 DeviceMetric instances necessarily lack that element unless transformed. The modifier flag also affects generated models, validation, and business logic because consumers must inspect status before relying on the resource. R6 values such as `active`, `inactive`, and `unknown` have no R4 DeviceMetric element to carry them.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misclassifying an entered-in-error metric as active device metadata could affect downstream device observation interpretation and audit behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate record lifecycle status from operational state and align DeviceMetric with resource status patterns.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Make `status` optional in the base resource or require it only in transition profiles.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: R6 separates record lifecycle from metric operational state and gives `entered-in-error`/`inactive` explicit modifier semantics. The 1..1 base requirement is disruptive, but the safety and consistency value of every DeviceMetric carrying lifecycle status makes the break probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have added `status` as 0..1 with best-practice guidance or profile-level requiredness. That would allow unchanged R4 instances to remain valid with respect to this element, but it would not let all base R6 consumers rely on lifecycle status and would leave modifier-sensitive state absent for legacy records.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances, but weakens uniform lifecycle/modifier handling and leaves inactive or entered-in-error safety optional.

evidence.detail: R4 differential has no `DeviceMetric.status` element.
R6 `status` is 1..1 code, required-bound to metric-status, summary, and modifier.
R6 metric-status defines active, inactive, entered-in-error, and unknown.
R6 adds a status concept map to generic resource-status, including entered-in-error to error.

examples.examplesMd: An R4 DeviceMetric fragment with only required R4 `type` and `category` still needs a newly derived R6 `status`; simply changing the FHIR version is invalid.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `DeviceMetric.status` as a mandatory modifier. This is a hard migration break because no R4 field can be copied directly for every instance: `operationalStatus` described whether the metric was on/off/standby/entered-in-error, while the new `status` describes the validity or lifecycle of the DeviceMetric record itself.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances become R6-invalid unless a 1..1 `status` code is supplied. Strict generated serializers and validators will require the new primitive. In the reverse direction, R4 has no status slot, so R6 `active`, `inactive`, and `unknown` are lost unless carried by extension or external conversion metadata.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define a policy for deriving `status`, commonly defaulting current usable records to `active`, mapping R4 `operationalStatus=entered-in-error` to `status=entered-in-error`, and using `unknown` only when lifecycle status genuinely cannot be determined. Test modifier handling explicitly, especially that entered-in-error records are not treated as active metrics.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is understandable because it separates lifecycle validity from operational state, but making the field mandatory in the base resource is disruptive. A transition-compatible alternative would have been optional base status plus profile-level requiredness or an invariant warning.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review defaulting rules carefully for historical or decommissioned metrics; an unconditional `active` default may be clinically or operationally misleading.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds `DeviceMetric.status` as a required modifier, so an unchanged R4 DeviceMetric will not validate and generated models must expose a new mandatory lifecycle field. The break is real, but the path separates record lifecycle from device operational state and gives entered-in-error/inactive status explicit modifier semantics. Given the low R4 maturity, this looks proportionate rather than a change that needs renewed design attention.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition has no `DeviceMetric.status` element.
R6 `DeviceMetric.status` is 1..1 code, required-bound to metric-status, `isModifier=true`, and summary.
R6 metric-status codes are active, inactive, entered-in-error, and unknown.
Lightweight web search found official/IG-level DeviceMetric and IEEE 11073 relevance, but no direct evidence of broad production deployment.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 DeviceMetric is FMM 1/trial-use, so the mandatory addition is not judged with mature-resource stability expectations. Safety relevance keeps it from being dismissed, but low FMM softens the concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen and R6-to-R4 loss: R4 instances lack the required field, R6 consumers must inspect the modifier, and R6 lifecycle values have no base R4 slot.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Making status optional in base R6 or requiring it only in profiles would preserve legacy instances, but it would defeat the goal that every base DeviceMetric carries computable lifecycle/modifier state. That tradeoff makes the less-breaking design only partially acceptable.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high hard-break assessment and partial alternative judgment, but the prior report overstates broad prevalence for an FMM 1 resource.

findings.title: R4 `source` and `parent` references are removed and replaced by mandatory `device`

oldState.summary: R4 had optional `source` and optional `parent`, both Reference(Device).
oldState.narrativeMd: `source` identified the Device containing administrative device information; `parent` identified the Device locating the metric in a containment structure.

newState.summary: R6 has required `device`, Reference(Device), and no `source` or `parent` on DeviceMetric.

semanticText.short: The device to which this DeviceMetric applies
semanticText.definition: The device to which this DeviceMetric applies. The referenced device could be a top-level device or a component of a device.
semanticText.comment: If the reference is not to a top-level device, the top-level device is reached through the device's `parent` element (possibly recursively).

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 model pushes containment hierarchy semantics to the referenced Device resource rather than keeping separate DeviceMetric source and parent links.

facts.note: Reference target stayed Device, but path/cardinality/semantics changed.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: R6 `device` appears to replace the combination of R4 `source` and `parent` because it is the only local Device reference and its comment explains top-level versus component Device hierarchy.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances that omit both references are invalid in R6 because `device` is mandatory, and R4 instances that contain `source` or `parent` use element names that no longer exist. Reverse conversion is ambiguous because one R6 `device` reference does not state whether it should become R4 `source`, R4 `parent`, both, or neither without inspecting the referenced Device hierarchy.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Wrong device association can attach measurements or settings to the wrong physical or logical device component.

justification.inferredGoal: Normalize DeviceMetric to a single subject Device and represent component hierarchy on Device.parent.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `device` while retaining deprecated optional `source` and `parent`, or make `device` profile-required during transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Normalizing DeviceMetric to a single referenced Device, with hierarchy represented through `Device.parent`, is a cleaner and more interoperable base model. The mandatory replacement is still highly breaking, but the old two-reference model had role ambiguity and no guaranteed device association.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A transitional R6 design could have retained `source` and `parent` as deprecated aliases while adding `device` plus precedence or consistency invariants. This would preserve many R4 instances, but it duplicates same-resource representations for the device relationship and risks conflicting links that implementers may support indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Improves compatibility, but creates duplicate device associations and ambiguity when `source`, `parent`, and `device` disagree.

evidence.detail: R4 `source` is 0..1 Reference(Device).
R4 `parent` is 0..1 Reference(Device).
R6 `device` is 1..1 Reference(Device).
R6 Device retains `Device.parent`, supporting the new hierarchy comment on DeviceMetric.device.

examples.examplesMd: A complete R4 instance with `source` and/or `parent` must be rewritten to R6 `device`; there is no same-name field preservation.

findings.narrativeMd: The Device reference model changed from two optional, role-specific DeviceMetric links to one required DeviceMetric link. This is both a validation break and a semantic migration problem: `source` and `parent` carried different R4 meanings, while R6 expects the referenced Device and its own parent chain to supply the context.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 content using `source` or `parent` will fail R6 validation because those elements are unknown, and content without a device reference fails the new 1..1 cardinality. R6-to-R4 conversion is not lossless without policy for splitting or duplicating the R6 `device` reference.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Choose a deterministic mapping rule. If R4 `parent` identifies the component that owns the metric, it may be the best R6 `device`; if only `source` is present, use `source`; if both are present and differ, inspect the Device hierarchy and preserve the other relationship on Device.parent or with an extension. Add tests for no reference, source-only, parent-only, and source-plus-parent cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The single-reference design is cleaner and probably aligns with Device hierarchy modeling, but preserving optional deprecated aliases or publishing a ConceptMap-like structural transform would have reduced migration ambiguity.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The exact source/parent-to-device mapping may depend on how an implementation represented channels, modules, or containment trees in R4 Device resources.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 removes R4 `source` and `parent` and replaces them with required `device`. This breaks R4 instances that use either old reference and also breaks instances that omitted both. More importantly, conversion can require deciding whether the correct R6 reference is the source device, a channel/component device, or a reconstructed Device hierarchy; the reverse direction is similarly policy-dependent. Because device association is central to interpreting a metric and wrong association can affect patient-monitoring context, this deserves renewed review despite low R4 maturity.
keyEvidence: R4 `DeviceMetric.source` is 0..1 Reference(Device) for the source/admin device.
R4 `DeviceMetric.parent` is 0..1 Reference(Device) for containment/location context.
R6 `DeviceMetric.device` is 1..1 Reference(Device) and states the referenced device may be top-level or a component.
R6 `Device.parent` exists as the hierarchy link for an encompassing device.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use softens the general compatibility burden, but this path is central to the resource's actual use and migration can be lossy or require expert policy. Those factors overcome the low-FMM discount.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus R6-to-R4 loss: old reference names are invalid in R6, missing the new required reference is invalid, and a single R6 device reference does not always map back cleanly to R4 source versus parent.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have added `device` while retaining deprecated optional `source` and `parent`, or made `device` optional during transition with consistency guidance. That would introduce duplicate relationship paths and conflict rules, but the tradeoff may be justified for a central association path.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high impact and partial-alternative analysis, but I judge the lossy central association change more concerning than probably justified.

findings.title: `operationalStatus` required value set removes `entered-in-error` and adds `unknown`

oldState.summary: R4 optional code with required binding to metric-operational-status including on, off, standby, entered-in-error.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: CodeSystem comparison used local complete CodeSystems rather than terminology server expansions.

semanticText.definition: Indicates current operational state of the device. For example: On, Off, Standby, etc.

newState.summary: R6 optional code with required binding to metric-operational-status including on, off, standby, unknown.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 status ConceptMap indicates entered-in-error moved conceptually to `DeviceMetric.status`, not operationalStatus.

semanticText.meaningWhenMissing: If absent, the operational status of the device is unknown.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because the binding is required, an R4 instance with `operationalStatus=entered-in-error` cannot keep that value in R6 `operationalStatus`. Conversely, explicit R6 `unknown` has no R4 required code; it could be omitted, but omission is not necessarily the same assertion.

justification.inferredGoal: Move record invalidity to the new lifecycle `status` element and keep operationalStatus focused on device operation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `entered-in-error` as a deprecated `operationalStatus` code while using `status` for lifecycle state.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving record invalidity out of `operationalStatus` and into mandatory modifier `status` is semantically coherent. The code removal is breaking for strict terminology validation, but continuing to allow a lifecycle/error code in a non-modifier operational field would undermine the R6 separation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have left `entered-in-error` in the required value set as deprecated, optionally with an invariant requiring `status=entered-in-error` when used. That would reduce validation breaks but is only a partial alternative because it preserves the old semantic overload and introduces contradiction risk between two status fields.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves rare old code values, but keeps operational and record-validity meanings mixed and can conflict with modifier `status`.

evidence.detail: R4 concepts include `entered-in-error`.
R6 concepts include `unknown` and no longer include `entered-in-error`.
R6 binding remains required.
R6 metric-status maps `entered-in-error` to generic resource-status `error`.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments are intentionally minimal and illustrate only the changed element, not a complete valid DeviceMetric.

findings.narrativeMd: `operationalStatus` keeps the same path and primitive type but its required value set changes. The old `entered-in-error` operational value is no longer legal there; R6 instead introduces `unknown` and uses the new `status` element for record validity.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is a direct terminology validation break for R4 instances that used `entered-in-error`. R6 `unknown` cannot be represented as an R4 operationalStatus code under the required R4 value set, although a converter could omit the element with some semantic loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map R4 `operationalStatus=entered-in-error` to R6 `status=entered-in-error` and usually omit R6 `operationalStatus` unless a real operational state is known. For R6-to-R4, decide whether `unknown` should become omission, an extension, or a rejected conversion.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is semantically cleaner but could have been phased by keeping the old code deprecated. Required bindings make code removal immediately breaking for strict validators.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The required value set for optional `operationalStatus` drops `entered-in-error` and adds `unknown`. This creates a validation break only for R4 instances that used the old entered-in-error operational code; the intended R6 representation is the new lifecycle `status=entered-in-error`, usually with operationalStatus absent unless a real operational state is known. The change cleans up a semantic overload and has a narrow affected instance set.
keyEvidence: R4 `DeviceMetric.operationalStatus` is 0..1 code with required binding containing on, off, standby, entered-in-error.
R6 `DeviceMetric.operationalStatus` remains 0..1 code with required binding containing on, off, standby, unknown.
R6 separately adds `DeviceMetric.status` with entered-in-error as a lifecycle status.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 1/trial-use makes a rare optional-code break less concerning, while the new status element provides a plausible migration target.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and R6-to-R4 loss: the old entered-in-error code is no longer valid for operationalStatus, and R6 unknown has no exact R4 required-bound code.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained entered-in-error as a deprecated operationalStatus code, but that would keep record validity mixed with operational state and create contradiction risk with the new modifier status. The less-breaking option has meaningful semantic cost.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing medium impact and partial alternative judgment, with low FMM further supporting that the break is probably acceptable.

findings.title: `category` changes from required primitive code to extensible CodeableConcept

oldState.summary: R4 required primitive `code`, required-bound to metric-category.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local CodeSystems show the same named category codes in R4 and R6: measurement, setting, calculation, unspecified.
Binding strength is weaker, allowing non-value-set concepts where needed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: `category` is mandatory in both versions, but the JSON/XML representation and generated type change from a primitive string to an object. R6 can carry text, multiple codings, and codings outside the value set under extensible binding; those cannot be losslessly represented in R4's single primitive code.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow richer and externally coded metric category representation while preserving the standard category value set as guidance.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep primitive `category` and add an optional CodeableConcept companion for richer category coding.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of allowing richer and externally coded metric categories is reasonable, and `CodeableConcept` is the idiomatic type for that goal. Replacing a required primitive is highly disruptive, but it avoids a long-lived pair of category fields representing the same fact.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `category` as a required code and added a new optional `categoryCodeableConcept` or similar element for additional codings/text. This would preserve all R4 category instances, but implementers would need rules for reconciling two category representations and the deprecated primitive could persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves the required R4 wire shape, but creates duplicate category representations and precedence/validation ambiguity.

evidence.detail: R4 `category` is 1..1 code with required metric-category binding.
R6 `category` is 1..1 CodeableConcept with extensible metric-category binding.
The core category codes are still measurement, setting, calculation, and unspecified in local R4/R6 CodeSystems.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows the essential wrapping transform; a full resource also needs other R6-required fields.

findings.narrativeMd: The category value did not merely get a new value set version; its datatype changed. This affects every DeviceMetric because `category` remains required. Existing R4 client code expecting a string enum must now handle a CodeableConcept with multiple codings and optional text.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An unchanged R4 JSON property such as `"category": "measurement"` is not valid R6 because R6 expects an object. R6 category content may not be reducible to one R4 primitive code, especially when only text or non-standard codings are present.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap standard R4 codes in `CodeableConcept.coding` with system `http://hl7.org/fhir/metric-category`. For R6-to-R4, prefer a coding from that system and a code available in R4; otherwise use an extension, manual mapping, or reject lossy conversion.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer type is likely useful, but a mandatory primitive-to-complex-type replacement is avoidably disruptive if backward wire compatibility is a priority. A transition element or cross-version extension would have reduced risk.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Because the binding was weakened from required to extensible, local profiles may need to restore stricter coding if downstream systems assume the R4 enum.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `category` remains mandatory but changes from a primitive code to a CodeableConcept with an extensible binding. That is a wire-format and generated-API break for every conformant R4 instance, but the core category codes are unchanged and straightforward R4-to-R6 migration can wrap the old code as a coding. R6-to-R4 can lose extra codings or text, but the change is a common enrichment of terminology representation rather than an obvious design error.
keyEvidence: R4 `DeviceMetric.category` is 1..1 primitive code with required metric-category binding.
R6 `DeviceMetric.category` is 1..1 CodeableConcept with extensible metric-category binding.
Local R4 and R6 metric-category code systems both include measurement, setting, calculation, and unspecified.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Because the R4 resource was FMM 1/trial-use, the mandatory wire-shape change is softened unless there is evidence of widespread production reliance. The field is central, but migration of ordinary R4 codes is mechanical.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: a primitive string representation is invalid where R6 expects CodeableConcept, and generated client/server types change.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping the primitive `category` and adding a richer companion element or choice would preserve R4 wire compatibility, but it would create duplicate representations and precedence rules for a required classification. The less-breaking design is plausible but not clearly better.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the prior report correctly identified a hard/API break and partial alternative, but its high impact should be tempered by low FMM and mechanical migration for the standard codes.

findings.title: `color` changes from R4 metric-color code to R6 CodeableConcept bound to color-codes

oldState.summary: R4 optional primitive code with required binding to metric-color's eight named colors.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: These code strings overlap with CSS color names, but the code system changes.

semanticText.short: black | red | green | yellow | blue | magenta | cyan | white

newState.summary: R6 optional CodeableConcept with required binding to color-codes, composed from color-names and color-rgb.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 color-codes includes 148 color-names plus a not-present RGB CodeSystem, so the R6 domain is much broader than R4's eight metric-color codes.

semanticText.short: Preferred color for displaying the metric
semanticText.meaningWhenMissing: If absent, there is no preferred color for rendering.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with `color` use a primitive string and an R4-specific code system; R6 requires a CodeableConcept and a different required value set. R6 can represent many color names and RGB values that cannot be reduced to the R4 eight-code domain.

justification.inferredGoal: Use a general FHIR color terminology and support richer color representations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the optional R4 primitive `color` and add a separate richer CodeableConcept color element, while mapping old names to the shared color terminology.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Using a shared color terminology and supporting RGB or broader named colors is reasonable. However, because `color` is optional display metadata and the R4 eight color names map naturally into a broader color vocabulary, replacing the primitive field was probably more breaking than necessary.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base R6 design could have kept `DeviceMetric.color` as the R4 primitive code, marked it deprecated, and added a new optional CodeableConcept field for richer colors. That would preserve existing R4 instances and still meet the core expressivity goal. The main tradeoff is duplicate same-resource color representations, but this is a moderate interoperability cost for display preference data rather than a central clinical/device identity field.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Creates some duplicate display-color representation, but the field is optional and low-safety, so the compatibility cost appears manageable.

evidence.detail: R4 `color` is 0..1 code with required binding to metric-color.
R6 `color` is 0..1 CodeableConcept with required binding to color-codes and is no longer summary.
R4 metric-color defines black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, and white.
R6 color-codes includes systems color-names and color-rgb.
R6 color-names contains 148 named colors, including the R4 color names as strings in a different system.

examples.examplesMd: Examples are focused fragments. R4 `blue` can probably map to R6 color-name `blue`, but no local ConceptMap confirms all mappings.

findings.narrativeMd: The color field changed both representation and terminology. Existing R4 primitive colors need object wrapping and a new coding system, while R6 permits many display colors that R4 cannot express.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 primitive `color` values are not valid R6 JSON as-is. Even after wrapping, validators will expect the R6 color-codes value set. R6-to-R4 conversion is frequently lossy outside the eight R4 names.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map the eight R4 metric-color codes to matching `http://hl7.org/fhir/color-names` codes when possible. For RGB or non-R4 named colors, use an extension or preserve the original R6 CodeableConcept outside the R4 base element. Test terminology validation against the R6 ballot package's color-codes ValueSet.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The broader color terminology is sensible, but omitting the old metric-color system or an explicit ConceptMap makes migration more brittle than necessary.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 `color-rgb` CodeSystem has content `not-present`; expansion behavior may depend on terminology server support for that code system.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `color` changes from an optional primitive metric-color code to an optional CodeableConcept using the general color-codes value set. Existing R4 instances with color need transformation, and many R6 colors cannot downgrade to the R4 eight-code domain. Still, this is optional display metadata with low safety weight, and the R4 color names map naturally into the broader R6 color-names system.
keyEvidence: R4 `DeviceMetric.color` is 0..1 code with required binding to eight metric-color codes.
R6 `DeviceMetric.color` is 0..1 CodeableConcept with required binding to color-codes and is no longer summary.
R6 color-codes includes color-names and color-rgb; color-names contains 148 named colors including black and blue.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use and the optional display-only nature of the field substantially reduce the need for standards reconsideration, even though instances using the field need a transform.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus R6-to-R4 loss: the primitive R4 code shape is invalid in R6 and expanded R6 colors or RGB values cannot always be represented in R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could have kept the old primitive `color` as deprecated and added a richer CodeableConcept color field. That alternative is real and relatively low cost, but it still introduces two color representations for optional display preference data.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree a less-breaking base design exists, but I would not carry forward the existing high impact concern for an optional low-safety FMM 1 path.

findings.title: `measurementPeriod` Timing is removed and replaced by `measurementFrequency` Quantity

semanticText.definition: Describes the measurement repetition time. This is not necessarily the same as the update period.

semanticText.short: Indicates how often the metric is taken or recorded
semanticText.definition: The frequency at which the metric is taken or recorded. Devices measure metrics at a wide range of frequencies...

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 element text and DIM mapping refer to measurement period/determination period semantics, making it the likely successor to R4 `measurementPeriod`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances containing `measurementPeriod` use an element name and datatype that no longer exist in R6. Timing can express schedules and repeats that may not reduce cleanly to a single Quantity frequency; R6 Quantity can express frequency-like values that may require constructing a Timing in R4.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent measurement cadence as a frequency Quantity rather than a general Timing schedule.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `measurementFrequency` while retaining deprecated `measurementPeriod` for transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Representing metric cadence as a frequency `Quantity` aligns with the R6 text and device mappings, and can be clearer for common sampling-rate use cases. The break is probably justified because a general `Timing` allows schedules that are not a single measurement frequency, but the replacement still leaves some R4 content needing review.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have introduced `measurementFrequency` alongside the existing `measurementPeriod` and deprecated the Timing form. That would preserve R4 instances and cover complex schedules, but it is only a partial alternative because two cadence fields can disagree, simple frequency and rich Timing semantics are not equivalent, and deprecated representations may accumulate.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 Timing schedules, but duplicates cadence data and creates conflict/precedence rules between Timing and Quantity.

evidence.detail: R4 `measurementPeriod` is 0..1 Timing and summary.
R6 `measurementFrequency` is 0..1 Quantity and not summary.
R6 mappings reference BICEPS DeterminationPeriod and DIM Measure-Period/update-period.

examples.examplesMd: The transform example is illustrative; exact Quantity coding depends on the source Timing and local unit policy.

findings.narrativeMd: The measurement cadence element was renamed and narrowed from general Timing to Quantity. This affects both instance shape and semantics: a Timing schedule is not always just a frequency value.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Any R4 instance with `measurementPeriod` is invalid against the R6 base resource until transformed. Some R4 Timing forms, such as complex day/time schedules, may not be representable as one R6 Quantity without losing detail.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Convert simple periodic Timing.repeat forms to UCUM-like frequency Quantities where possible, document assumptions, and route complex schedules for manual review or extension preservation. Include tests for simple hourly cadence, sub-second cadence, non-time-based cadence, and complex Timing patterns.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 model is clearer for metric frequency but could have been introduced alongside the existing Timing field to support gradual migration.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm the intended UCUM representation for frequencies in local implementation guidance; the base StructureDefinition does not bind `measurementFrequency` to a value set.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 removes optional `measurementPeriod` Timing and adds optional `measurementFrequency` Quantity. R4 instances that populate measurementPeriod do not validate without transformation, and complex Timing patterns may not reduce cleanly to one Quantity. The R6 definition and device-standard mappings indicate a narrower frequency/determination-period concept, so the design goal is plausible and retaining both cadence fields would create conflict rules.
keyEvidence: R4 `DeviceMetric.measurementPeriod` is 0..1 Timing and summary.
R6 `DeviceMetric.measurementFrequency` is 0..1 Quantity and not summary.
R6 mappings reference BICEPS MetricDescriptor/DeterminationPeriod and DIM Measure-Period or update-period.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Low R4 FMM softens the break, but the path can matter for device monitoring cadence. Because it is optional and the R6 model has a clear standards-mapping goal, the concern remains probably acceptable.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and possible R6-to-R4 loss: the old element name/type is gone, and Timing schedules and Quantity frequencies are not fully equivalent in either direction.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have added `measurementFrequency` while retaining deprecated `measurementPeriod`, but two cadence fields can disagree and Timing is broader than the R6 frequency concept. The alternative preserves more data but has non-trivial modeling cost.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing medium impact and partial alternative assessment, with explicit FMM tempering.

findings.title: Calibration type/state change from required primitive codes to extensible CodeableConcepts, with state code change

oldState.summary: R4 calibration `type` and `state` are optional primitive code elements with required bindings.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Calibration type codes are unchanged; calibration state replaces R4 `unspecified` with R6 `unknown`.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented calibration method and state as simple enum-like strings.

newState.summary: R6 calibration `type` and `state` are optional CodeableConcept elements with extensible bindings.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 permits richer calibration coding; `state` meaningWhenMissing says absence means unknown.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 supports coded concepts and non-core concepts where appropriate.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Instances with calibration type/state strings are not valid R6 without CodeableConcept wrapping. R6 can carry multiple codings or extensible concepts that R4 cannot reduce to one required primitive code. R4 `state=unspecified` also has no exact R6 core code; R6 uses `unknown`.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow richer calibration terminology and distinguish unknown from unspecified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain primitive calibration `type`/`state` codes as deprecated aliases and add optional CodeableConcept detail fields.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Richer calibration terminology is a reasonable R6 goal, and CodeableConcept with extensible binding supports local or standard calibration concepts better than primitive enums. The break is material, but avoiding parallel primitive and CodeableConcept calibration fields is a legitimate design reason.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have kept the R4 primitive `calibration.type` and `calibration.state` and added separate optional CodeableConcept fields, while deprecating `unspecified` or retaining it temporarily. This would preserve existing R4 calibration entries, but repeated calibration backbones would then have two representations for each fact and uncertain precedence when old and new codings differ.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Eases migration, but duplicates calibration facts inside a repeating backbone and complicates `unspecified` versus `unknown` semantics.

evidence.detail: R4 calibration.type is code with required metric-calibration-type binding.
R6 calibration.type is CodeableConcept with extensible metric-calibration-type binding.
R4 calibration.state is code with required metric-calibration-state binding.
R6 calibration.state is CodeableConcept with extensible metric-calibration-state binding.
R4 includes `unspecified`; R6 includes `unknown` instead.

examples.examplesMd: Mapping R4 `unspecified` to R6 `unknown` may be close but should be reviewed because the wording changed.

findings.narrativeMd: The calibration backbone remains, but two child elements change from primitive codes to CodeableConcepts. Calibration state also changes its unknown/unspecified vocabulary, which may affect validation and interpretation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 calibration strings are invalid R6 objects as-is. R6 calibration concepts outside the R4 value sets, or with multiple codings/text only, are not cleanly representable in R4. The `unspecified` to `unknown` change requires semantic review.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap calibration type and state codes using their HL7 code systems. Map R4 `state=unspecified` to R6 `unknown` only if the business meaning is acceptable; otherwise preserve the original code in an extension or alternate coding and flag for review. For reverse conversion, select one R4-supported coding or preserve the R6 CodeableConcept externally.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer representation is probably reasonable for calibration metadata, but it could have been phased through extensions or deprecated primitive fields.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Because bindings are extensible, local profiles may need to constrain allowed calibration codings if R4-style enum behavior is required.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Calibration entries still exist, but `calibration.type` and `calibration.state` move from optional primitive codes with required bindings to optional CodeableConcepts with extensible bindings, and state changes from unspecified to unknown. R4 calibration content needs structural wrapping and possible code mapping, while richer R6 codings may not downgrade losslessly. Because the backbone is optional and the ordinary code wrapping is straightforward, the break looks proportionate for an FMM 1 resource.
keyEvidence: R4 `DeviceMetric.calibration.type` and `.state` are 0..1 primitive code elements with required bindings.
R6 `DeviceMetric.calibration.type` and `.state` are 0..1 CodeableConcept elements with extensible bindings.
R4 calibration-state includes unspecified; R6 calibration-state includes unknown instead.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Calibration can be safety-relevant, but the affected children are optional and the resource was FMM 1/trial-use. That favors accepting a richer representation unless migration evidence shows broader harm.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen and R6-to-R4 loss: primitive calibration codes are invalid in the new shape, generated types change, and extra R6 codings/text may not collapse to R4 codes.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping primitive calibration type/state as deprecated aliases while adding CodeableConcept fields would preserve R4 instances, but it would duplicate facts inside a repeating backbone and require precedence rules, especially for unspecified versus unknown. The tradeoff is significant.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing medium impact and partial alternative judgment, while treating low FMM as a reason not to escalate.

findings.title: Several formerly summary elements are no longer marked `isSummary` in R6

oldState.summary: R4 marked color, measurementPeriod, calibration, calibration.type, calibration.state, and calibration.time as summary elements.
oldState.narrativeMd: These elements could be included by summary-aware serialization or REST `_summary` behavior in R4.

newState.summary: R6 marks color, measurementFrequency, calibration, calibration.type, calibration.state, and calibration.time as not summary.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 summary output focuses on status, operationalStatus, category, type, device, unit, availability, and identifiers.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This does not make instances invalid, but it can change REST `_summary` responses, generated summary views, indexing assumptions, and clients that relied on summary payloads containing color, cadence, or calibration data.

justification.inferredGoal: Reduce summary payload to core identifying/status fields.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep R4 summary flags stable, or introduce a separate lean summary convention instead of changing default summary membership.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The computable flag change is clear, but the local inputs do not explain why color, cadence, and calibration data needed to leave summary output. Because this is a runtime/client compatibility break rather than an instance-validity necessity, the justification is not clear.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The most compatible base design would keep the R4 `isSummary` flags and let systems that need smaller payloads use explicit element selection or a separately documented lean summary pattern. This is only a partial alternative because it does not deliver a smaller default R6 `_summary` response and may add operational variability.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves summary clients, but keeps default summaries larger or requires extra implementation conventions for lean payloads.

evidence.detail: R4 color is summary.
R6 color is not summary.
R4 calibration backbone and children are summary.
R6 calibration backbone and children are not summary.
R4 measurementPeriod is summary.
R6 measurementFrequency is not summary.

examples.examplesMd: A client using `_summary=true` to display DeviceMetric color or calibration state may stop seeing those values in R6 even though full-resource reads still contain them.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes summary behavior for several local fields. This is not a data validation break, but it is a practical runtime break for clients that use summary representations as lightweight device dashboards or lists.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Full instances remain valid based on content, but summary serialization can omit fields that R4 summary clients expected. This affects REST behavior and generated summary DTOs rather than base instance representability.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit clients and servers that rely on `_summary=true`, generated summary classes, or summary indexing. Request full resources or explicit `_elements` for color, measurementFrequency, and calibration data when needed.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been avoided by keeping summary flags stable, but summary selection is partly a design judgment about payload importance. The absence of narrative rationale limits assessment.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The summary-flag changes do not make any instance invalid and do not remove the underlying data from full resource reads. They can change default `_summary` payloads or generated summary views, but clients that need color, calibration, or cadence information can request the full resource or explicit elements. With an FMM 1 R4 resource and no evidence of production dependence on DeviceMetric summaries, this is metadata/runtime summary churn rather than a compatibility issue needing action.
keyEvidence: R4 marks color, measurementPeriod, calibration, calibration.type, calibration.state, and calibration.time as summary elements.
R6 marks color, measurementFrequency, calibration, calibration.type, calibration.state, and calibration.time as not summary.
No cardinality or datatype validation break is caused solely by the summary flags.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Low maturity strongly softens this non-instance-breaking concern; absent evidence of summary-response reliance, FMM 1 favors no action.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling with limited runtime/API summary behavior: `_summary` and generated summary views may differ, but base instances remain representable.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping the R4 summary flags would be more compatible for summary clients, but the compatibility benefit is speculative and would preserve a larger default summary surface. A separate lean-summary convention is implementation policy, not a necessary base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing medium runtime concern; the evidence supports a much lower practical risk and no need for revisit.

findings.title: R6 adds optional `availability` with no R4 representation

oldState.summary: No R4 base DeviceMetric element represented metric availability/continuity.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could only carry this concept by extension or external convention.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional `availability` CodeableConcept with extensible metric-availability binding.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding an optional element does not invalidate R4-to-R6 content, but R6 instances that use availability lose information when converted to base R4 unless an extension is used.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent whether a metric is continuous, intermittent, or unknown.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Optional additive R6 content is already forward-compatible for R4-to-R6 base validation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional `availability` is a reasonable way to represent metric continuity and does not invalidate R4 instances during R4-to-R6 migration. The compatibility issue is only that R6 instances using the new element cannot be represented in base R4 without extra machinery.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for the forward direction because the element is 0..1 and absent in migrated R4 data. For R6-to-R4 conversion, the practical mitigation is a cross-version extension or external mapping, which is a downgrade workaround rather than a backward-compatible base R6 alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No forward instance break; R6-to-R4 downgrade loses availability unless an extension or sidecar mapping is used.

evidence.detail: R4 DeviceMetric has no `availability` element.
R6 availability is 0..1 CodeableConcept with extensible metric-availability binding.
R6 metric-availability defines intr, cont, and unknown.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment cannot be represented in a base R4 DeviceMetric without extension.

findings.narrativeMd: `availability` is a useful additive R6 concept, but it creates a one-way conversion concern. R4 systems have no native place for continuous/intermittent metric availability.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is not broken by this optional addition. R6-to-R4 conversion loses the element unless an extension or sidecar mapping is used.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When downgrading R6 to R4, preserve `availability` in a cross-version extension if the receiving system needs the distinction. When upgrading R4 to R6, leave it absent unless availability can be derived reliably.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This is the least disruptive kind of change in the forward direction. Reverse compatibility necessarily requires an extension because R4 lacks the concept.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional `availability`; R4 content remains valid with respect to this path because the element can be absent. R6-to-R4 downgrade can lose availability if it is used, but that is a reverse-only information loss for new R6 content rather than a break in migrating R4 DeviceMetric instances.
keyEvidence: R4 DeviceMetric has no `availability` element.
R6 `DeviceMetric.availability` is 0..1 CodeableConcept with extensible metric-availability binding.
R6 metric-availability codes are intr, cont, and unknown.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use reinforces that an optional additive element with only downgrade loss should not be elevated.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss only: new R6 availability data has no base R4 slot, but R4-to-R6 validation is not broken.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed because the field is optional. Downgrade extensions or sidecar mappings are migration mitigations, not better R6 base designs.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing low impact and not-applicable alternative assessment.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, abstract flag, derivation, and DomainResource base are unchanged. Status changed draft to active and is recorded as a notable non-breaking metadata change.

Same-path local elements retained their min/max cardinalities. Cardinality impact comes from added/removed/replaced elements, especially required `status` and `device`, which are captured as findings.
All local DeviceMetric references in both versions target `Device`; the material change is reference role/path/cardinality, not target-profile narrowing or broadening.
No local DeviceMetric-specific invariant was added, removed, or changed. The root `dom-*` constraint expression changes are inherited DomainResource behavior and are out of scope.
No local fixed value, pattern, or default value constraints were found on DeviceMetric elements in either version.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue constraint change was identified.
No local slicing definitions were found on DeviceMetric in either version.
No existing same-path local element changed from non-modifier to modifier. The new modifier element `DeviceMetric.status` is captured as a finding.

Material serialization changes are captured where primitive code fields became CodeableConcepts and where element names changed. XML element ordering may also change because the R6 local element order differs, but this is secondary to the content-model changes.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is artifact governance metadata and does not by itself invalidate instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers may treat the R6 resource as more mature, but should remember the supplied R6 package is still a ballot build marked not for publication.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: `unit` preferred binding changed from devicemetric-type to ucum-units
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The binding strength remains preferred, so base validation should not reject instances solely because coding is outside the preferred value set.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology pickers, code generators, and conformance guidance should prefer UCUM units in R6, while the comment still allows UCUM or RTMMS/MDC-style coding.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Root narrative broadens DeviceMetric beyond the initial ISO/IEEE 11073 scope
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The root definition/comment change broadens applicability and does not impose a stricter validation rule.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems whose R4 assumptions were limited to ISO/IEEE 11073 context scanners should review whether R6 DeviceMetric may now appear in broader device contexts.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds BICEPS, DIM, and ACOM mapping metadata
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Mapping metadata does not change base instance validity.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The added mappings help explain source/parent/device, measurementFrequency, and terminology changes and may guide conversion tooling.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: The DeviceMetric snapshots show inherited `dom-*` invariant expression changes. Per scope, those should be assessed in the DomainResource/base-resource report rather than as local DeviceMetric findings.

R6 `DeviceMetric.device` relies on the referenced Device and its `Device.parent` chain to represent hierarchy formerly modeled partly through DeviceMetric `parent`; Device migration policy can affect correctness.
No local ConceptMap was found from R4 `metric-color` to R6 `color-codes`; strict terminology migration would benefit from an explicit map, especially for display-color semantics and RGB values.
Search behavior likely changes alongside the resource model, but SearchParameters are outside this assigned StructureDefinition report.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 DeviceMetric diff, Jira issue, or change note was available locally, so design justification and intended migration rules are inferred from computable definitions and mappings.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Official HL7 change notes or Jira tickets explaining DeviceMetric redesign decisions.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology comparison used local ValueSet compose and complete CodeSystem resources, not a terminology-server expansion. UCUM and color-rgb behavior may depend on terminology server capabilities.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Authoritative expansions for the R4 and R6 value sets, including color-codes and UCUM-related bindings.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Local status ConceptMaps were inspected, but no local ConceptMaps were found for source/parent-to-device, measurementPeriod-to-measurementFrequency, metric-color-to-color-codes, or primitive-code-to-CodeableConcept transforms.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Published cross-version maps or implementation guidance for DeviceMetric.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is `6.0.0-ballot4` from a package marked `notForPublication`; final R6 content may differ.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Repeat the comparison against the final published R6 core package.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No DeviceMetric example instances were found in either local core package, so prevalence estimates are based on element optionality and domain judgement rather than sample data.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Representative R4 production DeviceMetric instances or official examples.
